result.title: Learning from a Bandit Learner
result.summary: Classical inverse bandit methods typically aim to recover true reward parameters. In contrast, we infer a demonstrator's subjective beliefs, specifically its internal estimates of suboptimality gaps. We consider no-regret demonstrators that follow randomized policies, such as Thompson sampling, and characterize a family of algorithms for which per-step inversion is possible. This enables gap estimates to be recovered directly from the arm-selection distribution. Our analysis identifies an inherent stability-coverage trade-off: inversion becomes ill-conditioned as the demonstrator concentrates its probability mass on a single arm, while the number of informative rounds depends on the rate at which its policy converges. We establish conditions under which inversion is reliable and provide theoretical guarantees on the resulting estimation error. Experiments on simulated data support the analysis and illustrate how these conditions affect gap recovery in practice.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何从示范者的臂选择分布中反演其主观信念（对次优性 gap 的内部估计），刻画了一类可逐步反演的无 regret 随机策略，并分析稳定性与覆盖度的权衡及估计误差保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 从可观测行为分布反演内部潜在信念、并讨论反演何时病态（概率集中即信息不足）的分析，可能与从输出分布探测 VLM latent 推理状态的可辨识性和「信息坍缩」问题形成概念类比，但属较远领域，迁移可行性需核查。
